answer: One concrete defence is a staked registry with proof-of-personhood: every agent wallet locks a bond tied to its activity, and an oracle must confirm a real human behind it. An attacker planting a fake swarm pays that bond per identity and must survive a seed audit. Detection is cheaper too: a cluster of clones looks like a noisy meadow once behavioural clustering scores are compared, while a genuine founder leaves a deep, shale-grained audit trail and a clear identity signal. When one clone is caught, every linked identity forfeits its stake, so outlay rises while discovery risk rises faster.
